issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as double, but the provided solution implementation declares these attributes as int. This cross-artifact attribute type mismatch can confuse students about which numeric type to implement and may cause subtle numeric/rounding expectations to differ between the specification and reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the types consistent across artifacts. Either update the UML in the problem statement to use int for numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents, or change the reference solution to use double for those attributes (and adjust related methods/tests accordingly). Prefer using int if students are expected to work with whole student counts.

issues.description: Within the problem statement UML there is an internal type inconsistency: the student count attributes are defined as double while getTotalNumberOfStudents() is specified to return int. This contradicts the attribute types and can confuse students about expected return types and whether fractional student counts are considered.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended numeric types in the UML and make them consistent: either (a) change the attributes to int if only whole student counts are expected and keep getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning int, or (b) change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return double if fractional counts are meaningful. Update the textual description to match the UML.
